decisions.reason: The existing message-49 MODIFY already removes the obsolete Civic Canopy font source. The source does not establish a replacement font source or require another typography update.
Changing the proposal's brand identity does not alter the requirement to place photos in the final draft.
The branding shift does not change the requirement for layout treatment of the complete document.
This Requirement is independently introduced by message 49 and already records the Blue Mesa identity context and client-neutral prepared-for line; no additional propagated MODIFY is needed.
The selected brand identity does not change Canva ownership or editing access.
The branding decision does not change the requirement to include the organization chart.
The branding shift does not alter integration of the supplied tables into the current RFQ draft; modular table behavior is separately represented by the template Requirement.
Changing from Civic Canopy branding to Blue Mesa branding does not alter the 34-page limit.
The brand identity change does not alter the required PDF format or print-ready delivery condition.
The proposal must still package all required RFQ response content into one document regardless of its branding.
This Requirement concerns the separate RCP proposal, while the source decision applies only to the Civic Canopy RFQ proposal submitted by Blue Mesa Strategies.
The source decision concerns branding for a separate RFQ proposal and does not resolve or alter the optional graphics scope for the RCP proposal.
